subject: How is R-squared (R2, R^2) calculated in lavaan?

messages.author: 614751a2121381e1
messages.subject: How is R-squared (R2, R^2) calculated in lavaan?
parts:
I have used lavaan to perform path analyses for continuous dependent variables (CDV) as well as for a dichotomous dependent variable (DDV), and have been asked to report R-squared values for the CDV. I was able to obtain these using the "inspect(path.model,'r2')", but saw that R^2 is also given for the DDV. For consistency, I'd now like to report the R^2 for both the CDV and the DDV. However, I cannot find where/how these values are calculated. What kind of R-square is given for CDV and for DDV, and where are these values calculated?

Thanks for any help.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: How is R-squared (R2, R^2) calculated in lavaan?
parts: What kind of R-square is given for CDV and for DDV, and where are these values calculated?

In both cases, the R-squared is calculated as 1 minus the ratio of residual variance (appearing in the parameter estimates, although it might be a fixed value) to the model-implied total variance of that variable.  You can see the model-implied total variance using

lavInspect(fit, "cov.ov")

In the case of categorical (binary or ordinal) outcomes, lavaan uses a probit model that assumes there is a normally distributed latent response underlying the observed response.  Read these for details:

https://www.statmodel.com/download/webnotes/CatMGLong.pdf

https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10705510701758406

So the R-squared refers to the proportion of variance of that latent response that was explained by the predictors.
